title: Manifest-backed app plugins hide settings/health/resources/proxy unless compat flag is set
answers: Why did my app plugin's /health, /resources, /proxy or settings API disappear after adding a manifest?
How do I keep the legacy settings endpoint for a plugin that now ships an app manifest?
Plugin OpenAPI spec no longer lists app/instance routes for a manifest plugin
body:
Symptom: a plugin that gained an app manifest stops serving its settings CRUD, /health, /resources, /proxy subresources, and the v0alpha1 group version; its OpenAPI spec drops those paths too.
Root cause: pkg/registry/apis/appplugin/register.go:NewAppPluginAPIBuilder sets client and contextProvider to nil whenever plugin.Manifest != nil and FlagApppluginsLoadAppManifestAndKeepSettings is off.
Fix pattern: every place that conditionally wires settings must gate on the same b.includeSettings() check (client != nil && contextProvider != nil) defined in pkg/registry/apis/appplugin/openapi.go:includeSettings — GetGroupVersions (pkg/registry/apis/appplugin/register.go:GetGroupVersions), UpdateAPIGroupInfo's storage map, and PostProcessOpenAPI (pkg/registry/apis/appplugin/openapi.go:PostProcessOpenAPI) must all stay in sync with it.
Constraints: legacy (non-manifest) plugins always get settings; manifest plugins only get them if FlagApppluginsLoadAppManifestAndKeepSettings is enabled — a temporary migration flag, not a permanent per-plugin opt-in (reviewers noted a manifest-level flag may replace it).
applies: pkg/registry/apis/appplugin and anything that reads its OpenAPI/storage/version output for manifest-backed plugins
